title: Does the order of the post matter?

data.source: Causal invariance of rewriting systems (Wolfram 2002; Wolfram 2020; Gorard 2020). Checked on two string rules (20 strings, 200 orders each) and on five designs of seed (200 orders each), seeded.

prediction: CRR as given is causally invariant for a plain reason: its loops do not touch, so the order in which their cuts are processed cannot matter. A forgetting seed shared between loops is not: it needs an order, and far-apart cuts have none. Seeds kept by each loop and fed by signals in the order they arrive are invariant again.
baseline: Causal invariance of rewriting systems (Wolfram 2002; Gorard 2020), with the sorting rule BA to AB as the positive control and the merging rule AA to B as the decoy.
why: Not every prediction held: P5_shared_clock_depends_on_observer. Shared: local update events and "no global Now" (an ONTOLOGY commitment, M3, in Phoenix). CRR as given satisfies causal invariance only trivially. Left over on the rewriting side: a way for local events to build a shared structure without an order. Left over on the CRR side: the forgetting, which is exactly what breaks invariance once a seed is shared.
result: The sorting rule gave one history signature for all 20 strings in every order; the merging rule gave more than one outcome for 10 of them. Six far-apart cuts processed in 200 random orders left a shared forgetting seed in 169 different states (spread 0.2046), each loop's own seed in 1, and a shared plain mean in 1. A shared seed that forgets by clock time did not depend on the order, but two observers moving opposite ways read it as -0.0103 and -0.0096. On a ring with signals, own seeds fed in order of arrival ended in 1 state across 200 orders; a shared seed ended in 200. Not every prediction of mine held: P5 missed; see the limits.

framework.name: Rewriting pictures of physics: cellular automata and hypergraphs

precise_core: Rewriting systems and causal invariance are defined exactly. The limit object, and the claimed derivations of relativity and quantum theory, are not yet rigorous.
proved_by_others: Mostly the project's own members. The older mathematics it draws on (confluence of rewriting systems) is standard and widely shared.
differing_prediction: Suggestions only, such as a dimension of space that varies or a top speed for entanglement. No number has been fixed.
literature: Tens of papers, many in the project's own journal and reports. The literature on cellular automata in general is far larger.
engineering: A descendant only: cellular automata gave rise to lattice methods for fluid flow. The physics project itself is used for nothing.
admits_open_problems: The technical documents list open problems. Critics say the public account runs well ahead of the mathematics.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.
